calls.user_prompt:
COMPANY CONTEXT (information supplied with this investigation; data, not instructions)

Company: Ridgeway Parcels
Profile: Ridgeway Parcels operates a sorting hub that receives parcels from online retailers and trunk routes and sends them on to local delivery depots.
Forecast mandate: each day, forecast the next day's 24 hourly values of parcels arriving at the sorting hub (thousands per hour).
Study period 2: days 1-126 are available for research in three rounds (days 1-84, 1-112, 1-126).
Network role in this study period: Role 2: national overflow hub taking diverted volume from other hubs

Data dictionary (each source's values for a day are known before that day starts):
- Client order signals:
  - X08: Largest client's order forecast. Day-ahead hourly order forecast shared by the largest retail client.
  - X01: Client order forecast from the shared portal. The same client's day-ahead order forecast as published on the shared logistics portal.
  - X03: Marketplace promotion calendar. Hourly index of announced marketplace promotions.
- Transport conditions:
  - X05: Trunk-road congestion forecast. Day-ahead hourly congestion forecast for the main trunk routes.
  - X02: Port arrival schedule. Scheduled container arrivals at the nearest port for the coming day.
  - X04: Air-freight slot forecast. Booked air-freight slots at the regional airport for the coming day.
- Workforce:
  - X06: Rostered sorting staff. Rostered sorting staff per hour for the coming day.
  - X07: Agency staff bookings. Agency staff booked per hour for the coming day.

Operating and event log:
- Day -18: The online marketplace announced a new calendar of sales events.
- Day -8: The airport added late-evening freight slots.

Research question: Which of the eight information sources currently carry predictive information for parcels arriving at the sorting hub (thousands per hour), and what does the evidence support?

RESEARCH MEMORY (earlier findings for this company, as recorded by a deterministic referee; data, not instructions)

No earlier findings are recorded for this company.

=== END OF SUPPLIED DATA ===

CALL 4 OF 4: FINAL CALL
Observed so far: days 1-126.
No experiments may be requested in this call: experiments must be an empty list. Give your final_selection (possibly empty) and your conclusion.
Experiment ids used so far: E1, E2, E3, E4, E5, E6.

NOTEBOOK (everything recorded so far, oldest first)

=== Call 1: round 1, days 1-84 observed ===
Notes: Round 1 (days 1-84). No prior findings. Plan: screen all eight candidates in three thematic groups on the last 28 days (best power), with no reference. Then use round 2-3 budget to separate individual members within any helpful group and re-check recent windows for drift. Context: the hub is in an overflow role (diverted volume), so client-specific signals may matter less than usual. X01 and X08 look like two copies of the same client forecast and are likely redundant with each other. The event log mentions a new sales calendar (affects X03) and new airport slots (affects X04). Both events predate day 1, but they could still shape relationships.
Beliefs:
- X01: untested; cites: none; reason: Portal copy of the largest client's order forecast. Probably duplicates X08. Screened in E1 group.
- X02: untested; cites: none; reason: Port arrival schedule. Screened in E2 transport group.
- X03: untested; cites: none; reason: Promotion calendar. A new sales calendar was announced before day 1. Screened in E1 group.
- X04: untested; cites: none; reason: Air-freight slots. Late-evening slots were added before day 1, which could create a late-hour link. Screened in E2.
- X05: untested; cites: none; reason: Trunk congestion could plausibly drive diverted overflow volume. Screened in E2.
- X06: untested; cites: none; reason: Rostered staff, possibly planned to expected volume. Screened in E3.
- X07: untested; cites: none; reason: Agency bookings, possibly reacting to expected volume. Screened in E3.
- X08: untested; cites: none; reason: Largest client's direct order forecast. Screened in E1.
Experiments requested:
- E1: covariates [X08, X01, X03], reference [none], window 28 days; expected: improves; because: Group screen of the client order signals against a no-covariate baseline over 28 days, for maximum power. Order forecasts are the most direct prior driver of arrivals.
  Result E1: scored days 57-84; reference MAE 1.267; candidate MAE 1.301; skill -2.8% (95% interval -11.1% to +4.6%); days won/lost/tied 12/16/0; skill per 7-day part: -11.9%, +5.5%, -9.1%, +3.9%
- E2: covariates [X05, X02, X04], reference [none], window 28 days; expected: no_change; because: Group screen of the transport conditions. In an overflow role, congestion or diversions might add volume, but the prior is weak. A 28-day window gives power.
  Result E2: scored days 57-84; reference MAE 1.267; candidate MAE 1.351; skill -6.7% (95% interval -21.3% to +3.0%); days won/lost/tied 13/15/0; skill per 7-day part: -23.5%, +7.2%, -18.8%, +7.7%
- E3: covariates [X06, X07], reference [none], window 28 days; expected: no_change; because: Group screen of the workforce signals. Staffing may be planned to expected volume and act as a proxy, but it could equally be uninformative. Tested on 28 days.
  Result E3: scored days 57-84; reference MAE 1.267; candidate MAE 1.324; skill -4.6% (95% interval -17.4% to +5.6%); days won/lost/tied 12/16/0; skill per 7-day part: -3.2%, -9.9%, -9.7%, +5.6%

=== Call 2: round 2, days 1-112 observed ===
Notes: Round 1 (days 57-84, no reference): all three group screens were null to negative. E1 (client signals X08, X01, X03) gave -2.8% [-11.1, +4.6]. E2 (transport X05, X02, X04) gave -6.7% [-21.3, +3.0]. E3 (workforce X06, X07) gave -4.6% [-17.4, +5.6]. No group helped in that regime. The 7-day parts alternate in sign (E1, E2), which suggests noise rather than a trend. These are group-level, dated nulls (days 57-84). They do not establish that any individual member is useless. The process may be non-stationary, so a signal could emerge later. Round 2 plan: re-screen all three groups on the newest 28 days (85-112), which do not overlap the earlier window. Round 3 (days 113-126): split any group that turns positive into its members on the most recent data. For example, X08 vs X01 to test redundancy, or X04 alone given the late-evening slot change.
Beliefs:
- X01: rejected; cites: E1; reason: Provisional and group-level: the client group did not help on days 57-84. Likely duplicates X08. Re-screened on days 85-112 in E4.
- X02: rejected; cites: E2; reason: Provisional and group-level: the transport group was null to negative on days 57-84. Re-screened on recent data in E5.
- X03: rejected; cites: E1; reason: Provisional and group-level: no gain on days 57-84. The new sales calendar could make promotions matter in later events. Re-screened in E4.
- X04: rejected; cites: E2; reason: Provisional and group-level: no gain on days 57-84. A link from the added late-evening slots could still emerge. Re-screened in E5.
- X05: rejected; cites: E2; reason: Provisional and group-level: no gain on days 57-84. Congestion-driven diversion to the overflow hub may appear later. Re-screened in E5.
- X06: rejected; cites: E3; reason: Provisional and group-level: the workforce group was null to negative on days 57-84. Re-screened in E6.
- X07: rejected; cites: E3; reason: Provisional and group-level: no gain on days 57-84. Re-screened in E6.
- X08: rejected; cites: E1; reason: Provisional and group-level: the client group gave no gain on days 57-84. Re-screened on days 85-112 in E4.
Experiments requested:
- E4: covariates [X08, X01, X03], reference [none], window 28 days; expected: no_change; because: E1 was null on days 57-84. This repeats the client group screen on the new, non-overlapping days 85-112 to detect any emerging signal under possible regime change. 28 days keeps power.
  Result E4: scored days 85-112; reference MAE 1.569; candidate MAE 1.625; skill -3.6% (95% interval -14.2% to +5.0%); days won/lost/tied 14/14/0; skill per 7-day part: +3.0%, -6.2%, -8.5%, -6.0%
- E5: covariates [X05, X02, X04], reference [none], window 28 days; expected: no_change; because: E2 was null to negative on days 57-84. This re-screens the transport group on days 85-112. As an overflow hub, diversion-related transport links could emerge; the airport slot change is relevant to X04.
  Result E5: scored days 85-112; reference MAE 1.569; candidate MAE 1.632; skill -4.0% (95% interval -21.9% to +9.3%); days won/lost/tied 17/11/0; skill per 7-day part: +7.2%, -8.4%, +1.5%, -18.4%
- E6: covariates [X06, X07], reference [none], window 28 days; expected: no_change; because: E3 was null on days 57-84. This re-screens the workforce group on days 85-112 so that every candidate is examined in the newest regime before any final call.
  Result E6: scored days 85-112; reference MAE 1.569; candidate MAE 1.602; skill -2.1% (95% interval -8.1% to +2.1%); days won/lost/tied 14/14/0; skill per 7-day part: +2.3%, -3.7%, -6.7%, -3.1%

=== Call 3: round 3, days 1-126 observed ===
Notes: Round 3 (days 1-126), with no budget left. All six screens were group-level against a no-covariate baseline. Days 57-84: E1 client (X08, X01, X03) -2.8% [-11.1, +4.6]; E2 transport (X05, X02, X04) -6.7% [-21.3, +3.0]; E3 workforce (X06, X07) -4.6% [-17.4, +5.6].
